Syntax Error.why: Python needs punctuation, brackets, colons, and statement order to follow exact grammar rules.
Syntax Error.practice: Write five if/else blocks and intentionally remove one colon, then fix the error.

Name Error.why: A name error means Python saw a variable, function, or module name before it knew what that name referred to.
Name Error.practice: Create three variables, print them, then rename one safely everywhere it is used.

Type Error.why: Operations only work when the values involved have compatible types.
Type Error.practice: Convert strings to numbers before arithmetic in a small calculator program.

Runtime Error.why: Some problems appear only while the program is running with real values.
Runtime Error.practice: Add input checks to a program that divides two numbers.

Indentation Error.why: Python uses indentation to understand which statements belong inside loops, functions, and conditionals.
Indentation Error.practice: Write a loop inside an if statement and align every block with four spaces.

Import Error.why: Python must be able to find a module before your program can use it.
Import Error.practice: Import the math module and use three functions from it.

Index Error.why: Lists can only be accessed with indexes that exist inside their valid range.
Index Error.practice: Loop through a list using range(len(items)) and print each valid index.

Logical Error.why: A logical error means the code may run, but the result does not match the intended behavior.
Logical Error.practice: Write three test cases before coding a grade checker.
